requirements.requirement: On node1, serve a usable package repository whose content and metadata are stored locally.
requirements.summary: A signed tree RPM and generated repository metadata existed under /srv/repos/local. The enabled service listened on port 8080, returned the local repomd.xml over HTTP with an exact byte match, and DNF discovered tree exclusively through local-node1.

requirements.requirement: Install a package from the local repository while the usual remote repositories are unreachable.
requirements.summary: tree was initially absent. During installation, BaseOS, AppStream, and Extras all failed against a verified unreachable endpoint, while DNF selected tree from local-node1 and completed successfully. The installed executable worked and transaction history recorded provenance as @local-node1.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The mandatory node-restart protocol was also complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, restart was acknowledged, the boot ID changed, and the system, repository service, local content, DNF visibility, and installed package all recovered. The fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: Lifecycle snapshots are bounded rather than a complete filesystem and configuration audit.
Two small verification files were left in /tmp after evidence collection.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary state-changing commands were identified: package-tool installation, repository construction, service and DNF configuration, the target installation, and restart all had clear task or mandatory-evidence roles. The initially warned service identity was corrected before activation. Two bounded verification copies, /tmp/local-repomd.xml and /tmp/post-reboot-repomd.xml, remained after completion; these are minor executor-created residue rather than functional damage. Final observations showed no failed services and healthy package-manager state.
